parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Mission · Dewdney Trunk Road and Hayward Lake
Stave Falls is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Mission doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
City of Mission rezoning information packages list Stave Falls addresses such as 12412 Bell Street as City files, so Stave Falls is inside the City of Mission.
BC Parks gives access to Rolley Lake Park, in the Stave Falls area, as Bell Street north off Dewdney Trunk Road, and describes the park as 23 km northwest of Mission.
Hayward Lake, a BC Hydro reservoir on the Stave River, is on the area’s east side, with Ruskin Dam at its south end.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 18, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Mission and Mission Public Schools (School District 75).
General information only.

Recreation

blocks.text: BC Hydro Hayward Lake Recreation Area

parts.t: Has
BC Hydro lists a 90 m developed beach, a car-top boat ramp, wheelchair-accessible facilities and an off-leash dog area. Dogs are not allowed at the main beach
Safety
BC Hydro says lifeguards are at the designated beach area in peak season
BC Hydro page
Trail

blocks.text: BC Hydro and City trail Hayward Reservoir Trail

parts.t: Trails
Two out-and-back trails around Hayward Lake: the Reservoir Trail on the east side is hiking only and 10 km, and the Railway Trail on the west side allows hiking and cycling and is 6 km
Parking
Parking is first-come, first-served, lots often fill before 10 a.m., and there is no roadside parking
Closures
Parts of the trail pass through a working forest and may close during industrial operations
City trail page

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Stave Falls

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
On June 1, 2026 the City adopted Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026. That bylaw replaces and repeals Bylaw 6350-2025, a plan the City’s public notice calls substantively the same.
The City’s Stave West Interpretive Forest Master Plan covers the Stave West area, on the west side of Stave Lake.
The City’s Rural Mission Strategy was approved by Council on December 1, 2025, and names Stave Falls.

A City information package for 12412 Bell Street (about 3.1 hectares) says the property’s current OCP designation is Rural Residential and proposes rezoning from Rural 36 (RU36) to Rural Residential 7 (RR7). It says the RR7 zone has a minimum lot area of 0.7 hectares (1.73 acres).

BC Hydro’s safety notes for Hayward Lake say changes to Stave River water levels occur suddenly and without warning, flooding may occur in low-lying areas, and there are hazard areas above and below the Stave Falls and Ruskin dams.
BC Hydro says the City of Mission restricts parking along city roads leading to Hayward Lake.
I found no City page that gives a floodplain designation for specific Stave Falls properties.
I found no ALR mapping specific to Stave Falls on the pages I read.

In Mission, the District of Mission Land Use Inventory (2011) from the BC Government shows 1,539 hectares in the Agricultural Land Reserve, which is nearly seven percent of the land area of the District.
No route in BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley list is named for Stave Falls, and the same goes for the Mission routes numbered 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 and 39.
For a specific lot, send me the address and I’ll look up the zone and the plan designation.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Stave Falls

parts.t: Check the ALR status and the zone.
Check the Agricultural Land Commission map for the exact address. Then ask the City what the zone permits, such as how big a house can be and where it can sit.
Check the flood and slope rules.
Ask the City what the floodplain, drainage and hillside mapping mean for the exact address.
Check the water and septic.
Ask for well and septic records and the last inspection.
Check the road and access.
Ask whether the road is City-maintained and how the driveway connects, especially on a rural road.
Confirm the school catchment.
Ask School District 75 for the exact address; schools may be a drive away.
Get a full home inspection.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring.

FAQ
Where is Stave Falls?
Stave Falls is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Mission doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
City of Mission rezoning information packages list Stave Falls addresses such as 12412 Bell Street as City files, so Stave Falls is inside the City of Mission.
BC Parks gives access to Rolley Lake Park, in the Stave Falls area, as Bell Street north off Dewdney Trunk Road, and describes the park as 23 km northwest of Mission.
How do I get around from Stave Falls?
Stave Falls has no route named for it in BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley route list. None of the Mission routes there (31, 32, 33, 34, 35 and 39) carries the name either.
The nearest West Coast Express station is Mission City Station, at 33200 North Railway Avenue in Mission.

On weekdays, TransLink says, the West Coast Express runs between Downtown Vancouver and Mission City during the morning and evening rush hours. In the mornings it runs westbound only, while in the afternoon and evening it runs eastbound only.
Which schools are near Stave Falls?
Stave Falls Elementary, Kindergarten to 6, is at 30204 Brackley Ave.
SD75’s catchment policy puts Stave Falls Elementary in the Hatzic Middle School catchment.

On the Province’s list, the district’s senior secondary school is École Mission Senior Secondary, at 32939 7th Avenue, which serves Grades 10 to 12. Plans call for a replacement school with 1,500 seats on the same site, with Infrastructure BC showing the project as under construction.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
Mission Public Schools (School District 75)
, which publishes a catchment map.
What parks and trails are there?
Rolley Lake Provincial Park is reached by Bell Street north off Dewdney Trunk Road, and the Hayward Reservoir Trail has a 10 km east-side trail and a 6 km west-side trail.
The Powerhouse at Stave Falls visitor centre is listed as closed until March 1, 2027.
What plan covers Stave Falls?

Bylaw 6405-2026 is the Official Community Plan that the City adopted on June 1, 2026. It takes the place of Bylaw 6350-2025, which the City’s public notice describes as substantively the same plan, and repeals it.
The City’s Rural Mission Strategy names Stave Falls.
Is Stave Falls in a floodplain?

BC Hydro’s safety notes for Hayward Lake say changes to Stave River water levels occur suddenly and without warning, flooding may occur in low-lying areas, and there are hazard areas above and below the Stave Falls and Ruskin dams.
I found no City page that gives a floodplain designation for specific Stave Falls properties.
Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
